overview.title: Manueline heritage inside the walls
overview.p1: The Church of the Assumption is one of the rare examples of Manueline architecture still standing in Morocco. Built by the Portuguese in the 16th century, it stands in the heart of the citadel.
overview.p2: The sober façade and interior proportions recall the golden age of Portuguese expansion. It remains an active place of worship at times and a key stop on any heritage walk.
overview.p3: Combine it with the cistern and the ramparts for a full circuit of the Portuguese City.

q1.question: How much time for Church?
q1.answer: 30 to 60 minutes is usually enough for a good visit.

q2.question: Is there an entry fee?
q2.answer: Many outdoor areas are free; the cistern has a ticket. Check on site.

q3.question: Can I visit with children?
q3.answer: Yes, most sites are suitable for families with basic supervision.

q4.question: Is it open every day?
q4.answer: Outdoor sites are generally accessible daily; indoor sites may close one day a week.

q5.question: Do I need a guide?
q5.answer: Not required, but a local guide enriches the history of the Portuguese City.
